- Avoid over-optimism in early forecast periods; model tends to overestimate prices after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits persistent upward bias; apply downward correction of 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast exceeds 1.5x recent 10-day average, cap at 1.2x average.
- If sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model should not ignore recent low prices; adjust downward by 1–3% for 3–5 days post-low.
- Forecast should not diverge more than ±10% from 10-day moving average unless event-driven; otherwise, revert to historical mean.
